subject: Private cluster intake: sizing, node matrix and storage onboarding

Cc: ops@novamed.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster intake - initial requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting a private (on-prem) rollout for Novamed's inference stack and need Redwood's guidance on cluster sizing, node fleet breakdown, and storage patterns. High level:

- Peak inference QPS ~ 600 (burst to 1.2k) with typical request size ~ 350 tokens.
- Two environments: staging (small) and prod (primary).
- Model types: mix of 7B and 13B family (GPU-req), plus smaller CPU workers for embedders and async jobs.
- Data residency: all inference traffic must stay in our VPC; some sites will be air-gapped for compliance.
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted via customer-managed KMS/HSM; we need CSI + KMS guidance.
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime, p50 latency < 120ms for short prompt path.

Can you share what inventory and decisions you need from our side to produce a recommended node matrix and storage plan? I attached a very rough inventory (WIP).

Best,
Raj
Sr. Cloud Ops, Novamed

Raj / team — quick technical checklist and a recommended node matrix to guide the intake call. High-level assumptions: model-serving runtime supports batch and streaming; we can autoscale GPUs but prefer reserved pools for p50 SLA.

Checklist (info we can finalize on call):
- Exact model memory footprints (7B ~ 12–14GB FP16, 13B ~ 24–30GB FP16) + whether you want 4-bit quant variants.
- Latency SLOs for cold-start vs warmed KV-cache scenarios.
- Kubernetes version constraints and CNI (Calico / Cilium) preference.
- Storage snapshot/restore window for model artifacts (daily / weekly).

Initial node matrix (example for prod):
- control-plane: 3x m4.large (dedicated, no GPUs).
- infra/ops: 2x r3.large (monitoring, logging, ingress).
- gpu-small: 4x p3.8-like (4x A100-40GB) for 7B family (continuous warm pools).
- gpu-large: 6x p4d-like (8x A100-80GB) for 13B and batched workloads; can be mixed with pinned models.
- cpu-workers: 6x c3.xlarge (embeddings, pre/post processing, async jobs).
- burst-pool: 2x spot-capable GPU nodes for occasional bursts (if your procurement allows).

Storage guidance:
- Fast-local NVMe on GPU nodes for KV cache and kvstore (ephemeral, mount /tmp/kv).
- CSI block storage (encrypted) for model artifacts with the following: storageclass with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, reclaimPolicy: Retain, snapshot enabled.
- Shared model registry: object store (S3-compatible) on a network-accessible appliance; models pulled during bootstrap and cached to local NVMe.
- For air-gapped sites: signed model bundles + local object store mirror + offline KMS integration.

Network / security notes:
- Egress: allow only model artifact sync endpoints during scheduled windows; use NAT gateway with strict egress rules.
- Kerberos / mTLS between services for internal RPCs.
- Route Announcement: if multi-rack, we prefer BGP with local peering to minimize cross-rack hops for streaming.

I'll bring an ops-runbook draft and a CSI/KMS sample during the call. If anyone wants to propose different CPU/GPU SKUs, bring those procurement constraints to the call.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — Friday 7/3 at 10am PT works for me. A few answers up front:
- Concurrency split: ~70% short (<200ms) infer ops, ~25% medium batch requests (2–10s), ~5% long-running tuning jobs.
- Token budget: avg 350 tokens; 99th pct < 3k tokens. KV cache warm size estimate: 12–18GB per active GPU instance.
- KMS: Thales Luna HSM (customer-managed).
- Hardware: most DCs support NVMe; one regional site is limited to SATA-only.
- Air-gapped: yes, one site is air-gapped; we can accept signed tarballs and a one-time ship of images.

I've attached a slightly updated inventory and a brief procurement constraints doc (see drive link).
